controller_connection.title: E32 connection
controller_connection.description:
Connect this installation to your E32. You need two things first:

1. A broker login for the E32. With the Mosquitto broker add-on any Home Assistant user works: create one under Settings → People → Users → Add user (Users is shown when Advanced mode is on in your user profile), for example openthermostat with its own password.
2. The E32 on the broker: on its web page open System → Settings → Home Assistant → MQTT broker, tick “Connect to the MQTT broker”, enter the broker address (usually the address of Home Assistant), port 1883 and that user name and password, save and let the E32 restart.

No room is needed in Home Assistant: after connecting you add the rooms under Configure → Rooms, starting right here with the first one. The first connection may restart the E32 once.

The E32 password is stored with this Home Assistant integration. If you change it on the E32 later, Home Assistant asks for the new one. Connecting does not switch on heating control.

data_description.address: The address of the E32 in your network, for example http://192.168.1.50.
data_description.password: The password you sign in with on the E32 web page (user admin). A new E32 starts with admin; change it there under System → Password. Leave empty to keep the saved one.

data_description.name: The name you see in Home Assistant and on the E32. Up to 40 letters (fewer with accents or emoji); renaming keeps the room and its history.
data_description.state: On: the room can ask for heat. Heat along only: the room keeps its target and its radiator valves open for it, but it never asks for heat; it warms while the boiler runs for other rooms. Off: the room asks for no heat. For a temporary stop, set "Off until" below.
data_description.emitter: Radiators or floor heating. Floor heating warms up slowly and needs cooler water, so each type gets its own water temperature.
data_description.ha_sources: Thermostats or temperature sensors (°C or °F) in Home Assistant that measure this room. The first one with a fresh value is used; the others are backups. Drag to change the order. With one source: if it fails, the room stops asking for heat after 30 minutes. A second source, for example a Bluetooth sensor, covers that.
data_description.ble_sources: Sensors paired on the E32 itself; they keep working without Home Assistant.
data_description.bluetooth_first: On: the E32 uses its Bluetooth sensors before the Home Assistant sources.
data_description.setpoint_entity: Optional: a thermostat or radiator valve (for example a tado or TV02), or a number with a target, to set the room with. Home Assistant keeps it at the room's temperature; turning it changes the room (until the next switch time with a week program, for good without one). Turn off the device's own schedule (manual mode), otherwise it changes the temperature by itself. A device can be the room's setting device or a radiator valve the E32 drives, not both. Empty: no setting device; set the room with its thermostat in Home Assistant or on the E32 page.{setting_hint}
data_description.fallback_temperature: The temperature the room keeps when it has no week program, and while the E32's clock is not set yet. Without a week program a manual change becomes this temperature. On a room on Heat along only this is "Heat along up to": the valve opens up to it and the room asks for no heat itself.
data_description.program: Easiest: the visual planner under Week program on the OpenThermostat dashboard. This text is the advanced view of the same program: one line per group of days, for example mon-fri: 06:30 20.5; 22:30 18 and sat-sun: 08:00 20.5; 23:00 18. Temperatures in your Home Assistant unit. A line without days applies to every day. Up to 6 switch points per day; each temperature holds until the next point. Empty: no week program; the room keeps its temperature without a week program. A new room starts with the standard program "Workdays and weekend" (20 °C by day, 18 °C while away on workdays, 16 °C at night); clear the field if the room needs none.{resets_note}
data_description.resets: On that moment any manual change ends and the room takes this value; the E32 does not work towards it. At most four. One per line: the days, the time and a temperature or a state (on, heat along, off), for example mon-fri 22:00 14 or daily 09:00 heat along. In a room without a week program, give the evening reset time the temperature without a week program: then it also holds after a restart.
data_description.inactive_until: Only with Heating off: the date and time the room heats again by itself. Empty: off until you turn it on.
data_description.smart_warm_up: As the house: follows Smart warm-up of the house (Configure → Heating and boiler). On: this room is warm at its switch times. Off: this room starts heating at its switch times.

data_description.door_contacts: Doors you open often for a moment, such as the front door or the door to the garden. When one of them has been open for {door_delay}, the room pauses. A sensor is a window or a door, not both: move a door here from the window contacts.

energy.title: Energy and outdoor temperature
energy.description: Optional. With your gas meter, gas price, an outdoor temperature and your boiler's power the E32 calibrates its heat and gas estimates, and the heating advice shows savings in m³ and in your currency. Without them everything keeps working: estimates then use the burner power the boiler reports and a default boiler power, and the advice says what is missing. Leave a field empty to not use it.

data_description.gas_meter: A gas meter reading in m³ or kWh that only goes up (not a usage per hour), for example from a smart meter or a gas pulse counter. A reading in kWh is converted to m³ with the calorific value. It also splits your gas into heating and hot water for the Energy dashboard.
data_description.gas_price_entity: A sensor or input number with the gas price per m³ or per kWh (unit such as EUR/m³ or GBP/kWh). Use this or a fixed price, not both.
data_description.gas_price: The price per m³ of gas in your Home Assistant currency when you have no price sensor, for example 1.35.
data_description.gas_kwh_per_m3: Energy per m³ of gas; your gas bill or supplier states it. Empty: 9.77 kWh/m³ (Dutch gas). Elsewhere it differs, for example about 11 kWh/m³ in the UK; natural gas is usually between 8 and 12 kWh/m³.
data_description.outdoor_entity: A temperature sensor outside (°C or °F) or a weather entity. It helps the E32 learn how fast rooms cool down.
data_description.boiler_kw: The boiler's nominal heating power in kW (type plate or manual), 3–60 kW. Suggested: {boiler_kw_suggested} kW ({boiler_kw_basis}); empty keeps that suggestion.
data_description.water_meter: Optional: a water flow (L/min) or a water meter reading (m³ or L) that only goes up. With it, a hot-water round with water flowing is counted as tapping and one without as keeping warm, more reliably than from the boiler's temperatures alone. It stays in Home Assistant. With a hot water tank there is no such split: the E32 counts the taps itself.

device_own_schedule.title: {device} seems to run its own schedule
device_own_schedule.description: The target of {device}, the setting device of {room}, changed by itself at about the same time on several days. Home Assistant sets it to manual mode where it can; this one went back to its own schedule or has none Home Assistant can switch off. Turn off its own schedule in its app or under Settings → Devices & services (set it to manual mode): every change it makes by itself counts as a manual change of the room's temperature. This message goes away by itself once the device has not changed by itself for 8 days.

valve_two_roles.title: {device} was a setting device and a driven valve
valve_two_roles.description:
{device} was the setting device of {setting_room} and also a radiator valve the E32 drives in {room}. A device can be the room's setting device or a radiator valve the E32 drives, not both: the E32's own settings (8 °C during a pause, the warm-up target) would come back as a turn of its knob. Valve control of {room} is now off, so the valve opens and closes on its own sensor and follows what you set on it.

Choose what you want on the room's screen: Settings → Rooms → {room} on the OpenThermostat dashboard (without the dashboard: Configure → Rooms). Keep it as the setting device, or choose another setting device (or none) and switch valve control on again. This message goes away when you save the room.

setting_device_write_failed.title: {device} does not take the room's temperature
setting_device_write_failed.description:
Home Assistant could not set {device}, the setting device of {room}, three times in a row. Last attempt: {error}

Check that the device is on and set to heat, that it takes a target temperature (a thermostat with only a range gets its lower value), and that it still exists under Settings → Devices & services → Entities. This message goes away by itself as soon as setting it works again. To use another device, choose it under Setting device in the room's settings (Settings → Rooms → {room} on the OpenThermostat dashboard; without the dashboard: Configure → Rooms).

circuit_too_hot.title: {circuit}: water too hot, pump off
circuit_too_hot.description: The water to this circuit stayed more than 5 °C above its maximum for 2 minutes, so the E32 switched the pump off. Check the mixing valve. The pump starts again by itself once the water is below its maximum.

set_room_override.name: Temporary temperature for a room
set_room_override.description: A temporary target temperature for a room. Boost heats to the room's maximum (one hour unless you choose a duration). The E32 ends the temporary temperature itself, also after a restart, and the room returns to its week program or its temperature without a week program. Only the room's target temperature changes, never its state: a room that is off stays off and refuses it; the water temperature limits and frost protection stay.

mode.name: Kind
mode.description: Boost heats to the room's maximum; For a set time keeps the temperature for the duration; Until the next switch time keeps it until the next switch time of the room's week program (only for a room with a week program; E32 1.4.1 and older: at most 24 hours).

clear_away.name: End away
clear_away.description: Sets the house mode back to Automatic: every room follows its week program again.

end.description: Past end date and time with timezone. Choose an interval of up to 31 days.

e32_backup_unreachable.message: The E32 did not answer. Check that it is on and its web page opens, then try again.

e32_backup_password.message: The E32 refused the saved password. Enter the new one when Home Assistant asks for it (Settings → Devices & services), then try again.

e32_backup_update_required.message: The firmware on this E32 cannot make backups yet. Update the E32 first.

e32_backup_busy.message: The E32 is busy with a firmware update. Try again when it has finished.

e32_backup_failed.message: The backup of the E32 settings failed. Try again in a minute.

e32_restart_busy.message: The E32 cannot restart now: an update or the check of new firmware is running. Try again later.

e32_restart_failed.message: The E32 restart was not confirmed ({error}). Check the connection and try again.

house_holiday_too_many.message: At most 8 holidays can be planned. Remove one first.

firmware_download_failed.message: The firmware could not be downloaded from GitHub. Check the internet connection of Home Assistant and try again.

firmware_verification_failed.message: The downloaded firmware did not match the release (checksum). Nothing was installed.

firmware_upload_failed.message: The E32 did not take the firmware ({error}). Check that its web page opens, then try again.

firmware_not_confirmed.message: The E32 did not report the new version within 3 minutes. Check its web page; it may still be restarting.

firmware_release_unknown.message: This release is no longer offered. Check for updates again.

e32_not_connected.message: Home Assistant has no E32 connection yet. Connect it under Configure → E32 connection, then try again.

e32_not_reached.message: The E32 did not answer, so nothing was changed. Check that it is on and its web page opens, then try again.

e32_answer_unreadable.message: The E32 gave an answer this version cannot read, so nothing was changed. Update the E32 firmware and the integration together.

e32_update_required.message: The firmware on this E32 is too old for this. Update the E32 first (its Firmware update under Settings → Updates), then try again.

e32_busy.message: The E32 is updating or restarting. Try again once its web page opens normally.

shelly_rejected.message: The E32 refused the change ({error}). Nothing was changed.

shelly_unconfirmed.message: The E32 did not confirm the change. Try again in a minute.

shelly_unreachable.message: The E32 could not be reached to change the pump ({error}).

plan_confirm_unavailable.message: Home Assistant has no connection to the E32's settings, so it cannot confirm the plan. Connect the E32 in Configure first.

plan_confirm_unconfirmed.message: The E32 did not confirm that it plans the heating. Try again in a moment.

comfort_style_invalid.message: Choose comfort first, balanced or save most.

plan_confirm_refused.message: The E32 refused the confirmation ({error}). Look at its House page, or try again in a moment.

e32_relearn_failed.message: The E32 did not clear what it learned ({error}). Check the connection and try again.

e32_relearn_unknown_room.message: The E32 no longer has this room. Nothing was cleared.

e32_relearn_update_required.message: This E32 firmware cannot start learning again on request. Update the E32 first (Settings → Updates → OpenThermostat E32 Firmware).
